Frequently asked questions

What is an MCP Gateway

An MCP Gateway is a centralized control plane that securely manages access, discovery, and orchestration of MCP Servers across an enterprise. It acts as the operational backbone for agentic AI systems by enabling AI agents and applications to interface with enterprise tools via a standardized protocol. With support for authentication, RBAC, observability, and workflow execution in TrueFoundry, MCP Gateways make connecting and scaling intelligent systems seamless and secure.

What is an MCP Server and how does it work with the MCP Gateway?

An MCP Server acts as a standardized interface that wraps around enterprise APIs, making them callable by AI agents. Within TrueFoundry, each MCP server registers with the MCP gateway and becomes accessible through a unified endpoint. This connection allows your existing tools, such as Slack or Jira to inherit enterprise-grade features like RBAC and federated authentication, making multi-tool orchestration seamless.

How do I build and deploy an MCP Server?

You can build an MCP Server using TrueFoundry’s SDK or your preferred backend stack. MCP Servers are containerized and typically deployed on Kubernetes or cloud-native infrastructure. Once live, they register with the MCP Gateway and are made available for secure discovery and task execution via agents or users, streamlining the AI integration pipeline.

What are the key features of an MCP Gateway?

The MCP Gateway provides several key features for enterprises. It offers unified access to all registered MCP Servers, instant discovery via a central registry, and secure access control with OAuth 2.0 and federated identity providers. It enables agentic task execution across tools and, within TrueFoundry, it provides enterprise-grade observability with request-level tracing and audit logs. It also supports out-of-the-box and custom integrations (e.g., Slack, Datadog, internal APIs, among others), and ensures high-performance operation across cloud, on-prem, and hybrid environments.

What are the benefits of using an MCP Gateway in enterprise environments?

There are various benefits of using an MCP Gateway in enterprise environments. It dramatically simplifies tool integrations, accelerates onboarding via prebuilt MCP Servers, and unifies security and compliance controls. It enables plug-and-play agentic workflows, supports distributed environments, and provides deep observability for cost and performance. With TrueFoundry MCP Gateway, the result is a scalable, secure, and maintainable AI system capable of handling real-time enterprise workloads with minimal engineering effort.

How does the MCP Gateway handle authorization and access control?

Authorization in an MCP Gateway is enforced through Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) policies integrated with enterprise Identity Providers such as Okta or Azure AD. Each MCP Server, endpoint, or tool function can be governed by specific access rules, ensuring only authorized users or agents can trigger actions or retrieve sensitive data. TrueFoundry MCP Gateway streamlines this process by offering centralized authentication and secure orchestration.

Can I use my existing SSO or IdP with the MCP Gateway?

Yes, enterprise MCP Gateway and all MCP Servers like TrueFoundry fully support existing enterprise identity providers. Federated login via Okta, Azure AD, or custom SSO setups is supported out-of-the-box, enabling seamless integration into your organization's existing authentication and compliance stack.

What enterprise tools can I connect using MCP Servers?

You can integrate both standard and proprietary tools. For instance, the TrueFoundry MCP Gateway offers prebuilt MCP Servers for platforms like Slack, Confluence, Datadog, and Sentry. Additionally, you can create custom MCP Servers to connect any internal service, REST API, or data platform, extending orchestration across your unique tech stack.

How does MCP Gateway enable agentic task execution?

Through MCP Gateways like TrueFoundry, AI agents can autonomously discover, authenticate, and call MCP Servers. This enables them to execute multi-step workflows (e.g., “create a Jira ticket from Slack messages”), generate and run code, or orchestrate tools, all governed by standardized interactions and enterprise policies.

What kind of observability does the MCP Gateway offer?

An MCP Gateway provides full visibility into every interaction with MCP Servers. It supports end-to-end tracing, metadata tagging (e.g., team, user, tool), and audit logging for compliance. For example, through the TrueFoundry MCP Gateway, enterprises can monitor latency, usage, errors, and cost attribution in real-time, ensuring traceability and control across AI workloads.

Is the MCP Gateway secure and scalable for enterprise deployment?

Absolutely. MCP Gateways are designed for production-grade deployments. They support federated SSO, OAuth 2.0, dynamic discovery, multi-region failover, and role-based security, all while operating at high throughput under real-time enterprise load. It’s built to power large-scale, AI-first systems with confidence. TrueFoundry reinforces this posture by supporting secure deployments across private VPC, on-premise, and air-gapped environments.
